name: @hypersoniclabs/helix-mcp

tools.name: get_started
tools.description: REQUIRED FIRST STEP before building any HELIX Instant world. Returns the complete project recipe. Pass kind="character" for a world with a player character in ANY camera framing — all built on the humanoid-character system. Pass kind="multiplayer" for a world where players share a space and/or a game — presence PLUS declarative game logic (scores, teams, entities, physics, turns); returns the multiplayer HUB that routes to 12 worked templates + the multiplayer-logic DSL (you write no server code). Pass kind="scene" for a bare scene with no character. Omit kind to get the decision guide.

kind.description: "character" = humanoid-character world; "multiplayer" = shared world (presence + declarative game logic; the hub + 12 templates + the DSL); "scene" = bare world; omit for the decision guide

tools.name: read_doc
tools.description: Read a HELIX Instant reference document: "character-world", "multiplayer-world" (shared-presence worlds: join flow, replicas, sendState), "multiplayer-logic" (the declarative game-logic DSL: declared state, when/if/then rules, entities, zones, timers, state machine, collections, ownership), "sdk" (full @hypersoniclabs/helix-sdk API), "manifest" (every helix.json field + bundle rules), "publishing" (pipeline, login, error semantics), "catalog" (platform systems/abilities/asset-packs).

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List the available multiplayer world TEMPLATES — complete, publish-shaped worked worlds, one per capability cluster (presence, server/owned/shared/physics entities, collections, state machine, time, checkpoints, teams). After get_started({kind:"multiplayer"}), pick the closest and read it with read_template({name}).

tools.name: read_template
tools.description: Read a complete, publish-shaped multiplayer world template: its DSL checklist, the full public/helix.json (incl. the multiplayer block), the client src/main.ts delta, and build/publish steps. Pick the name from the hub (get_started multiplayer) or list_templates — e.g. "hangout".

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Check HELIX login state. Publishing requires a logged-in creator account; if not logged in, drive the browser sign-in with start_login (the human completes it on the website).

tools.name: start_login
tools.description: Begin the HELIX browser sign-in for the production environment (https://helixgame.com): opens the human's browser to the sign-in page and returns the URL — relay it if the browser did not open. The human completes the sign-in on the website; the minted token is captured and saved locally by this process (never returned to you). Poll check_login for the outcome. No-ops when already logged in to this environment.

openBrowser.description: Open the human's browser automatically (default true); false = only return the URL to relay

force.description: Sign in again even when already logged in to this environment (switch accounts)

tools.name: check_login
tools.description: Check the outcome of a start_login flow: pending (the human is still signing in — wait and re-check), done (logged in; credentials saved), or failed (timeout/denied — start_login again to retry).

tools.name: validate_world
tools.description: Validate a built world bundle directory (the Vite dist/ folder containing helix.json) against the exact rules the platform enforces at publish. Run this after building and fix every reported problem before publishing.

directory.description: Absolute path to the built bundle directory (e.g. the dist/ folder)

tools.name: publish_world
tools.description: Publish a validated world bundle to HELIX Instant. Uploads the files and activates the build; returns the public play URL. Requires login (check whoami first). Re-publishing the same slug creates the next build of that world.

directory.description: Absolute path to the built bundle directory (e.g. the dist/ folder)

tools.name: set_preview_video
tools.description: Set (or clear) a published world's preview video from a YouTube link. It plays as an extra slide in the world detail carousel; the world's thumbnail stays the cover. Video is REFERENCED, never uploaded — there is deliberately no way to upload an mp4/webm (the preview slot takes images only; YouTube does the transcoding, streaming and moderation). Accepts any usual shape — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ID, https://youtu.be/ID, /embed/ID, /shorts/ID, /live/ID, or a bare 11-character id; extra params like &t= are discarded. The link is normalised and host-checked server-side, so a non-YouTube URL is rejected rather than stored. Requires login (check whoami first) and a world you own — publish it first, then set its video.

slug.description: The world slug (as published; see list_my_worlds)

url.description: YouTube link or bare video id. Omit together with clear:true to remove the video.

clear.description: Remove the world's preview video instead of setting one

tools.name: list_my_worlds
tools.description: List the worlds owned by the logged-in creator (including drafts), with their slugs and build state.

tools.name: import_character
tools.description: Convert an external biped character GLB (a Meshy AI export, or any Mixamo-named rig) into a helix-humanoid@1 character asset. Conforms the mesh onto the canonical skeleton AT ITS OWN PROPORTIONS (the platform’s shared locomotion clips then drive it), generates the LOD chain (micro-chart baked atlases are auto-rebaked: weld → re-unwrap → closest-point texture transfer), and KTX2-encodes the textures — all in-process, no native tools, no extra files (the canonical helix-humanoid@1 skeleton is bundled; a world’s installed humanoid-character pack or `canonical` overrides it). Outputs <output>/<name>.web.glb (multi-scene: scene i = LOD i; the head is sliced into a FaceMesh node per level so first-person mode can hide it, like the stock face part), plus <output>/anims/<clipName>.glb when `anim` is given. Use when the human supplies a custom character model instead of the stock bodies. Validated example — a Meshy AI character with its walk animation, everything else default: { "body": "C:/downloads/Meshy_AI_Warrior_biped_Character_output.glb", "anim": "C:/downloads/Meshy_AI_Warrior_biped_Animation_Walking_withSkin.glb", "name": "warrior", "output": "./characters" } → characters/warrior.web.glb (~3MB, LOD tris ≈10000/5000/1500 at 1024/512/256px KTX2, UASTC up close + ETC1S far) + characters/anims/locomotion.warriorWalk.glb.

body.description: Absolute path to the source biped character GLB (skinned body)

anim.description: Optional animation GLB on the SAME source rig — retargeted onto the canonical skeleton

canonical.description: Canonical helix body GLB override; omit to use the world’s installed humanoid-character pack when present, else the bundled helix-humanoid@1 skeleton

worldDir.description: World directory searched for the installed pack and used as the base for a relative `output` (default: cwd)

name.description: Output basename → <name>.web.glb (default: derived from the body file name)

texSize.description: Texture longest-edge cap, halved per LOD level (default 1024)

lodTris.description: Triangle target per LOD level, high→low (default [10000, 5000, 1500])

tools.name: install_world_packages
tools.description: Resolve a world's helix.json system/ability pins against the platform catalog, download their code into public/helix_modules/, and wire the hosted three runtime (import map + src/helix.runtime.ts). Run it in the world project after `npm install` and after every pin edit, before `npm run build`. Replays the committed helix.lock.json when present; pass update:true to re-resolve ranges to newer versions and rewrite the lock. Same code path as the human `helix install`, but resolution happens in-process against THIS toolchain's environment — no PATH ambiguity.

directory.description: Absolute path to the world project directory (the one containing helix.json or public/helix.json)

update.description: Re-resolve pins against the live catalog and rewrite helix.lock.json (default: replay the existing lock)

tools.name: list_systems
tools.description: List the runtime systems published on HELIX Instant (e.g. humanoid-character). A system is a versioned framework that hosts abilities; a world pins one. Returns slug@version + title.

tools.name: list_abilities
tools.description: List the abilities published on HELIX Instant (e.g. fly, swim). Abilities plug into a system; optionally filter by the host system id. Returns slug@version + title + target system.

system.description: Only abilities targeting this system id (e.g. humanoid-character)

tools.name: get_package_manifest
tools.description: Fetch the full manifest for a published system/ability/asset-pack — the contract to read before pinning OR configuring it. For a SYSTEM, the payload carries `config` (the complete tunable surface) + `capabilities`. For an ABILITY, ability.json with its configSchema. Always includes the code + asset CDN base URLs. Defaults to the latest version. Read this instead of guessing config keys.

version.description: Semver version; defaults to the latest published version

tools.name: check_for_updates
tools.description: Check whether the HELIX @helix toolchain is current: compares the installed CLI / MCP / SDK / manifest against the latest published on npm and returns the exact update command for any that are behind. Pass the world/ability project dir to also check its pinned deps (e.g. @hypersoniclabs/helix-sdk).

projectDir.description: Absolute path to a world/ability project, to also check its pinned @helix dependencies

instructions:
HELIX Instant: build browser worlds with AI and publish them to a play-from-a-link platform.
ALWAYS DISCOVER FIRST: before designing a world, call list_systems + list_abilities to see what is already published — the catalog grows, so reuse a published system/ability instead of rebuilding it.
NEVER GUESS SETTINGS OR CAPABILITIES — read them. get_package_manifest returns the full tunable surface + what a package can do: for a SYSTEM, `config` (every tunable with defaults/ranges: camera modes, body, locomotion, …) + `capabilities` (input actions, blackboard conventions, built-in abilities, API); for an ABILITY, ability.json incl. its configSchema. Read it before you pin OR configure a system/ability — do not invent config keys.
TUNABLES LIVE IN THE MANIFEST `config`, NOT THE TYPESCRIPT CLASS API. Speed, spawn, look-sensitivity, initial look direction, FOV, slope, jump feel — almost everything a designer reaches for is a config VALUE, not a method. If you inspect the Character/LocomotionAbility class and conclude "no setting for X exists", you looked in the wrong place — re-read the manifest `config`. Set values two ways: initial via `Character.create({ config: { locomotion: { runSpeed: 7 }, character: { spawn:{x,z}, camera:{ mode, initialYaw, lookSensitivity } } } })`, or live via `character.config.set("ns.key", value)` (read every tick — use it for timed buffs, re-facing, difficulty). Runtime-only actions (teleport/applyImpulse/respawn/setEnabled/camera.setYaw/addTrauma) are in `capabilities.api`. The character-world recipe has worked examples (timed speed-boost, camera re-face, top-down/2.5D).
MATCH THE CONTROLS TO THE GENRE — every `allow*` gate DEFAULTS TO ON, so you must DISABLE what does not fit, or the player keeps a control the game should not have. A first-person game MUST set `character.camera.allowModeToggle:false` or pressing T still flips to third-person; top-down sets `allowRotate:false`+`allowZoom:false`; a no-jump walking sim/puzzle sets `locomotion.allowJump:false`. Pick the camera mode AND lock the gates that contradict it whenever you configure a character.
PICK THE FOUNDATION: if the world has a player character — ANY camera framing: first-person, third-person, 3D top-down (twin-stick/ARPG/MOBA), 2.5D / side-on (platformer), an avatar that walks/runs/jumps, or behaviors like fly / swim / shoot — build on the humanoid-character system: call get_started({ kind: "character" }). Top-down & 2.5D are just camera/movement config on this system. If players must SEE EACH OTHER or share a game (a hangout, co-op, an arena, a shared-object game), call get_started({ kind: "multiplayer" }) — the hub: a capability-indexed template index (then list_templates + read_template for a complete worked world) plus the declarative game-logic DSL (read_doc multiplayer-logic). You write no server code. For a bare scene with no character, get_started({ kind: "scene" }).
THEN BUILD: follow the recipe get_started returns EXACTLY (do NOT guess the format) → generate the files → npm install → install_world_packages on the project dir (any world that pins systems/abilities; resolves the pins in-process against THIS environment) → npm run build → validate_world on dist/ and fix every problem → whoami (not logged in? start_login opens the browser sign-in for the human, then check_login) → publish_world on dist/ for the public play link.
Deeper references via read_doc (character-world, multiplayer-world, multiplayer-logic, sdk, manifest, publishing, catalog). For shared game state beyond presence (scores, teams, server objects, rules) read multiplayer-logic. Run check_for_updates to confirm the toolchain (CLI/MCP) + a project’s @hypersoniclabs/helix-sdk are current.
